title: Have AI do it, then edit anything
notes: ONE band, worded once, placed on every product, segment and solutions page (AGL-2921). It is in its own file and its own directory because the copy format had no way to say 'this block is shared': `product-copy/copy-<page>.json` and `solutions-copy/copy-<page>.json` are each one page's own sections, and `apply-page-copy.js` pours one file into one canvas. The alternative was the same six strings pasted into twenty-five files, where the second edit forks them silently — the failure this directory exists to prevent. Nothing imports this file yet; it is the authoring source the besigner pass reads, the same way `product-copy/` is.
sharedBy: Every page in `targets`. The wording is page-neutral on purpose: a band that says something different per page is not one band, and the moment it takes a per-page variable it becomes twenty-five files again.

slotContract.notes: The flatten a band-aware applier would use, in document order, in the same shape as the section contracts in `apply-page-copy.js`. The disclosure is the LAST slot so that removing it at flip time is a trailing node deletion and a slot count of 4 — nothing else moves.

heading: Have AI do it, then edit anything.
body: Describe what you want and Aglyn AI builds a draft from your own theme, layout and components. It never publishes, never changes a live page and never sends anything — you do, through the buttons you already use.

disclosure.body: Rolling out — Aglyn AI is a release-flagged feature and does not appear in every workspace yet.
disclosure.notes: Required while `release_ai_generative` is off in production, where every generative route answers 404: a band saying 'have AI do it' on twenty-five live pages, with no qualifier, is twenty-five misrepresentations rather than one. Same wording family as the docs' `:::caution Rolling out` admonitions and as the notice band on /product/ai, so all three come off together — see `project_release_ai_generative_flip_sequence`. It is its own text node, its own slot, and the last one, so the flip deletes it rather than rewriting the band.

placement.position: Directly above the page's Explore band (section 5 on a product page), below How it works.
placement.rationale: Late enough that the page has said what the product is before it offers to build it for you, and adjacent to the other cross-sell band so the two read as one hand-off rather than two interruptions.
placement.besigner: Build it ONCE as a reusable component and place an instance on each target, rather than twenty-five copies of the same section. That is what this file is for on the canvas side, it is what the platform's own building rules tell a customer to do with a block that repeats, and it makes the flip-time deletion one edit to one component instead of twenty-five.
placement.ordering: ⛔ POUR THE PAGE COPY FIRST, THEN PLACE THE BAND. `apply-page-copy.js` asserts the canvas has exactly as many root sections as the 8-section contract and refuses to write anything otherwise, so a page carrying the band is a page the applier will no longer pour. To re-pour a page later, remove the band, pour, place it again. `verify-applier.mjs` carries this as a negative control so the constraint is checked rather than remembered.

notTargeted.why: This band's destination. A band linking a page to itself is a dead link, and the hub says all of this at length.
Has its own AI add-on row and its own guards; a band that names a capability beside a price table invites a figure into a surface `docs/PRICING_SURFACES.md` already counts nine of.
Comparison pages concede only code-verified gaps, so an AI claim there is an `/alternatives` row with a dated competitor fact beside it, not this band.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Aglyn AI builds a draft from your own theme, layout and components
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED. 'From what you already have' is the rule the generator is actually held to: a plan that creates something the site already has is refused, and a color the theme lacks is proposed as a theme change rather than authored as a literal.

claimsToVerify.phrase: It never publishes, never changes a live page and never sends anything
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED, and this clause is the reason the band can carry an imperative headline at all. 'Have AI do it' without it reads as an agent acting on a live site. It is three of the four nevers from the hub page; the fourth (never registers an address, never touches navigation) is dropped for length, not because it is untrue, and the three kept are the ones a reader of a product page would worry about.

claimsToVerify.phrase: Have AI do it, then edit anything
claimsToVerify.source: AGL-2921 title; keyword plan §2 — the `/alternatives/*` AI row reads 'Describe it, get a draft, edit anything'
claimsToVerify.concern: RESOLVED as wording, with one thing to hold: 'do it' must never grow an object that is not released. It is deliberately intransitive. A per-page variant — 'Have AI write your workflow' on /product/workflows — would claim a door that is shut (`apps/docs/docs/ai/automations-with-ai.md#draft`), and it would also stop this being one band.

OPEN UNTIL THE FLIP, on every page carrying the band. The flip is a four-part change and the flag is the last part; a band published without this line before then is wrong on twenty-five pages at once, which is the whole argument for one component and one instance per page.
